selection_framework.strength: Record yield and ultimate strength against exact product form, heat treatment and temperature.
selection_framework.stiffness: Titanium's modulus is much closer to steels than aluminium; mass reduction therefore does not imply proportional stiffness reduction for equal geometry.
selection_framework.fatigue: Surface finish, residual stress, notch geometry, mean stress, microstructure and manufacturing route are critical.
selection_framework.fracture: Toughness and crack-growth behaviour must be linked to alloy, product form, orientation and test environment.
selection_framework.creep: Relevant for near-alpha and other elevated-temperature grades; time-at-temperature evidence is mandatory where applicable.
selection_framework.bearing_and_fretting: Contact conditions can dominate performance; surface treatment and preload must be considered.

screening_comparison.CP_titanium: lower strength / excellent corrosion / high ductility
screening_comparison.Ti-6Al-4V: balanced strength, fatigue and corrosion / general-purpose high-performance titanium

design_rule: Do not use a family-level strength number as a design allowable.
